held_out.what: Leave-one-creator-out prediction of the engagement change, GAIL v1 predictor, 99 creators
held_out.verdict: does not beat the simple baselines (improvement over always-zero +0.13, interval -0.06 to +0.38)

acceptance.what: scripts/gail_acceptance.py on synthetic worlds: tests the OLDER estimator (GAIL v1)
acceptance.verdict: not accepted: the old estimator under-estimates a planted effect (dense) and is wrong in the sparse worlds; the newer GAIL-R is evaluated by the benchmark below

benchmark.what: Semi-synthetic: the real creator graph (390 creators, 354 collaboration edges) with an effect planted only through collaboration edges; 10 repetitions
benchmark.caveat: the effect travels only through the edges GAIL can see, so this favours GAIL; real data is noisier and the effect, if any, may not follow collaboration edges

benchmark_hard.what: Same real graph, weaker planted effect and noisier outcomes (real control changes have sd 0.88); mean absolute error of the estimated mean effect, 10 repetitions each; the mean true effect is small because only creators with a sponsored collaborator carry the effect
logs: semisynth hard runs of 30 Oct (effect 0.25 / 0.5 at noise 0.9 / 1.5)
benchmark_hard.reading: At realistic noise (1.5) GAIL-R's error (about 0.05) is as large as the true mean effect (0.06 to 0.11), and with a pre-trend even the placebo-penalised version errs by about 0.11: effects this small could not be told from zero. The older GAIL v1 errs by 0.14 to 0.25 throughout.

held_out_gail_r.what: Held-out check of GAIL-R itself on the extended graph (60 exposed): 5-fold split by creator, 20 repetitions; does its effect term reduce error on creators it never saw?
held_out_gail_r.verdict: no: the effect term does not help on unseen creators (median gain -3.2%; the wrong-window control is -1.8%). Earlier: 19 exposed -3.8% vs -1.5%; 12 exposed -3.4% vs -5.4%; 11 exposed -1.8% vs -1.8%.

multiseed.what: GAIL-R with learned attention over 10 seeds on the extended graph (60 exposed, 93 creators), plus a creator-level bootstrap
multiseed.verdict: the estimate is near zero in every seed (-0.16 to +0.09) and the interval [-0.40, +0.40] includes zero, about half as wide as with 19 exposed. Earlier: 19 exposed mean -0.28; 12 exposed -0.29; 11 exposed -0.54.

assumptions.planted_trend: normal, mean 0.15, sd 0.15 per neighbour, added to the lift after the event and at placebo dates

sim_lag_power.how: extra attention of s x the creator's own mean rate x 24 h, spread over 12-36 h after each real Instagram post; detection = smallest after-event p < 0.0125 (4 windows, Bonferroni)

claude_text_only_readings.note: Two Claude passes (15 Oct draft, 26 Oct pre-labels) reading only the description or caption, NOT human checks. Text alone cannot hear a spoken sponsorship or see the video, so this is a lower bound on how many are real ads; the one-by-one human checks above are the reference.

label_quality.scoring_rule: tier precision from human checks, shrunk toward pooled 0.973 with 5 pseudo-checks

label_noise.reading: Even if 30% of the comparison group were truly exposed, the upper end of the 95% interval stays below a 1.3x engagement effect; the null is not an artefact of a moderate number of missed labels.
label_noise.limits: homogeneous effect; random missing labels; a correct exposed group; this is a sensitivity table, not the full mismeasured-treatment model
